status: Projects now has a bounded native project-detail and WBS milestone/dependency read, an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport, and a configured SSR cutover. The Projects owner remains partial: shared composition mounting, the root workspace-member registration, purchase-atomic owner reads, project graph/task/actuals/handoff reads, commands and browser acceptance remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice reads the current project row and its bounded milestone hierarchy, parent links and predecessor dependencies. Task assignment, project graph tasks, approved time, posted costs, attachments, handoffs, project commands and the other four Projects workflows are not claimed.
scope.domain: Project read actor policy (records.read, Projects module, selected-context expiry), Company and exact project identity, bounded project/milestone row shapes, parent existence and cycle detection, dependency existence and cycle detection, depth and dependency-count limits, completion/timestamp consistency and computed overdue state.
scope.application: One project_wbs use case requires the current actor before any repository call, rejects non-member/hidden projects with PROJECT_NOT_FOUND, validates every owner row against the actor Company and requested project, and computes overdue state from the caller's current timestamp.
scope.adapters: Own SQL over staff_projects, staff_project_members, staff_project_milestones and staff_project_milestone_dependencies only. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required. Project visibility and IAM same-person aliases use the existing iam_same_person projection. No task, People, Finance, purchase, IAM mutation or workflow SQL is invented; no owner write is performed.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/projects/{project_id}/wbs. Exact Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS origin validation, duplicate/unknown query rejection, bounded project identifier validation, private/no-store and no-referrer responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company scope, purchase admission and serializable owner read.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_PROJECTS_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact project/milestone/context shapes, unique milestone IDs, parent/dependency references and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader.
scope.ssr: The Projects detail presenter uses the native project and milestone rows when the native configuration is present. An unset ERPX_NATIVE_PROJECTS_CONFIG retains the legacy project/milestone reader so existing development and tests remain usable; once configured, an invalid or failed native read is surfaced rather than silently replaced.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next owned wrapper keeps the retained requireProjectPurchasedRead preflight ahead of the native read. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current authority and purchase admission on its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No browser journey, authenticated page render, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, catalogue registration, command/idempotency receipt, audit/outbox effect, project graph/task/Finance/People/Inventory guard, handoff, attachment, job, production or staging acceptance.
